name: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
features: A glass tent-like atrium leans on a white tower with cantilevered drum and box volumes over the lake.
note: year was design start; opened 1995

name: Wembley Stadium
features: A tilted steel arch carries much of the roof, letting movable roof panels open over the pitch.
note: year was construction start; opened 2007; designed with Populous

name: Museum of Modern Art
features: Galleries layered around a tall atrium look onto the sculpture garden through refined glass and stone.
note: year was institution founding; Taniguchi's rebuilding opened 2004 (later DS+R expansion 2019)

name: Art Gallery of Ontario
features: A long curved glass-and-Douglas-fir galleria wraps the old museum; a sculptural timber stair spirals up.
note: year was institution founding; Gehry's transformation opened 2008

name: Torre de Collserola
features: A slim concrete shaft held upright by tensioned guy cables carries a stack of triangular decks.

name: Miho Museum
features: Approach through a tunnel and over a cable-stayed bridge to glass-roofed halls set into a mountain.

name: Mode Gakuen Cocoon Tower
features: An elliptical tower of schools wrapped in a white web of curving diagonal bands, like a cocoon.

name: Fernsehturm Berlin
by: Hermann Henselmann, Fritz Dieter and Günter Franke
features: A tapering concrete shaft carries a steel-clad sphere holding a viewing deck and revolving restaurant.
note: year was construction; opened 1969; Dieter and Franke added as designers

name: Ibirapuera Park
note: a park; better to add its buildings (Oca, Bienal Pavilion, Marquise) one by one

name: Whitney Museum of American Art
features: An asymmetric steel-clad block steps back in outdoor terraces toward the Hudson beside the High Line.
note: year was institution founding; Piano's building opened 2015

name: Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles
features: Red sandstone cubes, pyramid skylights and a barrel vault frame galleries sunk below a plaza.
note: year was institution founding; Isozaki's building opened 1986

name: Abeno Harukas
note: commercial supertall of limited design interest

name: Pergamon Museum
features: A three-winged neoclassical block built around reconstructed ancient monuments like the Pergamon Altar.
note: year was construction start; completed 1930 by Hoffmann after Messel's death

name: Art Institute of Chicago, Modern Wing
features: A floating 'flying carpet' of aluminium blades filters north light into the top-floor galleries.
note: Piano designed the Modern Wing (2009), not the 1893 building; renamed and year corrected

name: JPMorgan Chase Tower
note: commercial office tower of limited study interest

name: John F. Kennedy Presidential Library and Museum
features: A white concrete triangle and cylinder meet a tall black-framed glass pavilion facing the harbour.

name: Serpentine Galleries
note: an institution; Hadid designed only the Serpentine Sackler Gallery extension (2013), which would need its own entry

name: One World Trade Center
note: commercial tower of limited design interest

name: Palace of Culture and Science
features: A stepped Socialist Realist tower and spire, dressed with attics borrowed from Polish Renaissance towns.

name: Space Needle
features: Paired steel legs pinch in at a waist, then flare out to carry a disc-shaped top house.
note: year was construction start; opened 1962

name: Metro Bilbao
note: a whole metro network; the Foster glass station entrances could be a separate entry

name: Palau Sant Jordi
features: A domed space-frame roof was assembled on the ground and jacked into place over the Olympic arena.

name: Museum of Pop Culture
features: Colourful blobs of painted aluminium and stainless steel shingles flow around the passing monorail.
note: year corrected to opening (2000)

name: Opéra Bastille
features: Layered curved facades of glass and grey stone step around the Place de la Bastille.

name: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
features: A stepped brick-clad block split by a striped stone cylinder that lights the atrium from above.
note: year was institution founding; Botta's building opened 1995 (Snøhetta expansion 2016)

name: Riverside Museum
features: A zigzag pleated roof spans a column-free shed open at both ends, between the city and the river.

name: Palazzo Lombardia
features: Sinuous office ribbons wrap a central tower and enclose a covered public piazza.

name: Stadio San Nicola
features: Upper stands split into concrete petals with gaps between, floating over a bowl set in an earth bank.

name: Statue of Liberty
note: a statue, not a building; architect credit wrong (Bartholdi sculptor, Eiffel structure, Hunt pedestal)

name: Tokyo Tower
features: A steel lattice tower painted in international orange and white, modelled on the Eiffel Tower.
note: year corrected to completion (1958)

name: Bode Museum
features: A neo-baroque museum on the tip of Museum Island, its domed entrance rising straight from the river.

name: Messeturm
features: A pencil-like tower of red granite and glass, shifting from square shaft to cylinder to pyramid cap.
note: year corrected to completion (1991)

name: Gewandhaus
features: A glazed foyer shows off a huge ceiling painting to the square, in front of a fan-shaped concert hall.
note: year was construction start; opened 1981

name: Museum Folkwang
features: Pavilions and courtyards linked by glazed walkways, clad in translucent panels of recycled glass.
note: year was institution founding; Chipperfield's building opened 2010

name: Mudam
features: Glass-roofed halls rise from the arrow-shaped walls of an old fortress, Fort Thüngen.

name: World Trade Center
note: a building complex (destroyed 2001), not one building

name: Central Park
by: Frederick Law Olmsted and Calvert Vaux
note: a park without a key building

name: Woolworth Building
features: A Gothic Revival skyscraper of terracotta over a steel frame, with a mosaic-vaulted lobby.
note: year corrected to opening (1913)

name: Torre Emperador Castellana (Torre Espacio)
features: A square plan at the base morphs into two curved faces as the glass tower rises.

name: Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden
features: A hollow concrete drum raised on four piers rings a fountain court beside a sunken sculpture garden.

name: Palau de les Arts Reina Sofia
features: A sweeping cantilevered steel crest arcs over shell-like volumes clad in white broken-tile trencadís.

name: Central Market Project (World Trade Center Abu Dhabi)
note: commercial mixed-use towers of limited design interest

name: Solow Building
features: Travertine-edged glass curtain walls sweep down in concave curves to the street on two faces.

name: Gruppo Mondadori
note: a publishing company, not a building; Niemeyer's Palazzo Mondadori (1975) would need its own entry

name: Bellesguard
features: A slate-clad neo-Gothic villa with brick-vaulted attics and a tower topped by a cross.
note: year corrected to completion (1909)

name: Lyndon Baines Johnson Library and Museum
features: A windowless travertine block with a broad overhanging top floor stands over a raised plaza.

name: Philharmonie Luxembourg
features: A concert hall ringed by a dense screen of slender white steel columns in an eye-shaped plan.

name: Museum Tinguely
features: A pink sandstone block with a glazed walkway, the 'Barca', running along the Rhine into the galleries.

name: Eiffel Tower
by: Gustave Eiffel (with Koechlin, Nouguier and Sauvestre)
features: A wrought-iron lattice whose four curving legs gather into a single tapering shaft.
note: credited to Eiffel's firm; Sauvestre was its architect; year corrected to completion (1889)

name: Palais Garnier
features: A Beaux-Arts opera whose grand staircase and foyers make a promenade as theatrical as the stage.
note: year was construction start; opened 1875

name: Tretyakov Gallery
note: an institution; Vasnetsov designed only the facade of the older building

name: Lusail Stadium
note: generic stadium of limited design interest

name: NEMO Science Museum
features: A copper-green hull rises from the harbour over a road tunnel, its sloping roof a public stepped square.
note: year was institution founding; Piano's building opened 1997

name: Oscar Niemeyer International Cultural Centre
features: A white dome, a curved auditorium and a slim tower stand on an open riverside plaza.

name: L'Auditori
features: A gridded concrete-and-steel block of concert halls is organised around a glazed central lantern court.

name: Israel Museum
features: Modular stone-clad pavilions step down a hillside like a Mediterranean village.
note: Dora Gad added as co-designer

name: American Museum of Natural History
by: Calvert Vaux and Jacob Wrey Mould
note: an institution complex of many wings; Vaux's original building is largely hidden

name: Vienna State Opera
by: August Sicard von Sicardsburg and Eduard van der Nüll
features: A neo-Renaissance opera house with an open loggia facing the Ringstrasse and a grand staircase.
note: van der Nüll added as co-architect

name: Altare della Patria
features: A white marble monument of stairs and a curved colonnade crowned by bronze quadrigas.

name: MetLife Building
by: Emery Roth & Sons, Walter Gropius and Pietro Belluschi
features: An elongated octagonal slab of precast concrete set across the axis of Park Avenue above Grand Central.
note: credit corrected (TAC was Gropius's firm; Emery Roth & Sons and Belluschi co-designed)

name: Palasport Olimpico
note: generic arena of limited design interest

name: de Young Museum
features: A perforated, dimpled copper skin wraps low galleries and a twisting tower in Golden Gate Park.
note: architect field was an ID; year was founding; Herzog & de Meuron building opened 2005

name: Museum of Fine Arts, Houston
note: an institution of several buildings; Mies designed only Cullinan Hall and the Brown Pavilion

name: Philharmonie de Paris
features: A shell of interlocking bird-shaped aluminium tiles rises to a rooftop belvedere above the park.

name: High Museum of Art
features: White enamel-panelled galleries wrap a quarter-circle atrium lit from above and climbed by ramps.
note: year was institution founding; Meier's building opened 1983

name: Amon Carter Museum of American Art
features: A shellstone portico of tapered arches faces a terraced plaza looking toward downtown.

name: Auditorium Parco della Musica
features: Three beetle-like halls with lead-clad roofs ring an open-air amphitheatre.

name: Kunsthalle Bielefeld
features: A compact cubic block clad in red sandstone, set beside a sculpture garden.

name: World Port Center
note: commercial office tower of limited design interest

name: National Museum of Anthropology
features: A vast umbrella roof on a single sculpted column, ringed by falling water, shades the central courtyard.

name: National Gallery of Canada
features: A glazed colonnade ramp climbs to a crystalline Great Hall that echoes the Library of Parliament.
note: year was institution founding; Safdie's building opened 1988

name: Plenitude Arena
note: generic event venue; not sure of the building's details

name: Bergisel Ski Jump
features: A concrete tower carries a café and ramp that merge into one continuous, flowing form.
note: year was the old jump's; Hadid's jump opened 2002

name: Pampulha Modern Ensemble
note: an ensemble of buildings; the Church of St Francis of Assisi would be the key entry

name: Citigroup Centre
note: commercial office complex of limited design interest

name: University of Brasília
note: an institution/campus; the Central Institute of Sciences would need its own entry

name: 53W53
features: A tapering tower wrapped in an irregular exposed diagrid that ends in crystalline peaks.
note: year was design; completed 2019

name: IDS Center
features: A zigzag-cornered glass tower with a Crystal Court of stacked clear cubes linking the skyways.

name: Museum für Moderne Kunst
features: A wedge-shaped 'piece of cake' plan fills a triangular site, with galleries around a toplit hall.
note: year was founding; Hollein's building opened 1991

name: Jacob K. Javits Convention Center
by: I. M. Pei & Partners (James Ingo Freed)
features: A dark glass skin on a vast steel space frame encloses the halls and a crystal-palace-like lobby.
